subject: Aurelia Health — sponsor readout: objectives, risks, procurement runway
messages:
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
To: Emily Chen <emily.chen@aureliahealth.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Aurelia Health — sponsor readout: objectives, risks, procurement runway

Emily — thanks for the time today. Quick written recap so we have the same set of expectations across sponsors and the procurement path. Notes from our call (edited for clarity):

Pain / current state:
- Intermittent latency spikes on peak clinical queries (95th percentile > 1.2s) that are impacting clinician workflow.
- Cost leakage on large batch jobs when models are used outside of peak windows; current infra is hard to predict.
- Regulatory constraint: PHI handling needs demonstrable controls and a VPC/private deployment option.

Goals (what success looks like for Aurelia):
1) Run a 6-week pilot in Q1 that integrates with the triage assistant (non-production data) to validate latency and throughput SLAs.
2) Evaluate two model variants (base + quantized) and demonstrate token-cost reduction of >=30% without measurable drop in clinical precision on our test prompts.
3) Establish an operational handoff/playbook for production cutover and an explicit data residency plan.

Procurement path and timeline we discussed:
- Pilot SOW (technical scope + 6-week acceptance criteria) — target sign by Jan 15 (CFO approval window per your note).
- Legal review (standard Redwood MSA + data annex) — expect 7–10 business days once we have initial SOW and SOC2 evidence.
- Post-pilot: option to convert to Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs) with a 60–90 day lead for provisioning.

Open risks & escalation items:
- SOC 2 scope and any subprocessor list for the pilot environment (you asked for specifics).
- Data residency requirement for production (if Aurelia requires on-prem or specific cloud region, it will affect provisioning).
- Procurement cadence — if CFO decision slips beyond Jan 15 we should plan a model fallback to hosted with encryption-in-transit and strict access controls to keep timelines.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Logan: draft pilot SOW and acceptance criteria (ETA 2026-12-21).
- Kimberly: pull SOC2 scope extract and subprocessor list (ETA 2026-12-20).
- Marissa: prepare a cost-vs-latency comparison of the two model variants for the triage workload (ETA 2027-01-05).

I attached a one-page summary deck and a SOC2 extract stub; will follow with the pilot SOW doc tomorrow. Please reply with any changes or if I misunderstood priorities.

Thanks —
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
logan_wright@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0132
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Aurelia_Call_Summary_20261218.pdf (summary deck), SOC2-scope-extract.pdf (requested scope stub)

From: Emily Chen <emily.chen@aureliahealth.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir.patel@aureliahealth.com>
Date: 2026-12-18T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Aurelia Health — sponsor readout: objectives, risks, procurement runway

Logan — thanks for the crisp recap, that mirrors our notes. A couple of clarifications: 

- Budget: CFO has reserved a pilot allocation but will sign only after we receive SOC2 evidence and a simple pilot SOW. He is targeting a decision by Jan 15; we will keep you posted if that slips.
- Procurement lead: Samir (copied) will own routing through our legal/procurement. Samir, can you confirm if Aurelia requires internal PO before DocuSign?
- Subprocessors: can you provide the current list — especially any cloud providers or analytics vendors used in telemetry? We can accept a redacted list if necessary.

Also, please include an explicit line in the SOW that the pilot environment will not store patient-identifiable elements (we will run de-identified flows).

Emily Chen
VP Clinical Operations, Aurelia Health
emily.chen@aureliahealth.com | +1 617-555-4472

--
Emily Chen
Aurelia Health

Kimberly/Marissa — following Emily's asks, here are concrete owners and timing. I've quoted Emily below for context.

> "Please include an explicit line in the SOW that the pilot environment will not store patient-identifiable elements (we will run de-identified flows)."

Action items: 
- Kimberly: SOC2 scope extract + subprocessor list (redacted acceptable). Please surface any subprocessor contracts that might require our legal to sign a separate flow-down. ETA EOD 2026-12-20.
- Marissa: run the cost/latency sim for the triage workload (include base vs quantized; show P95 latency and estimated token costs for a 6-week pilot). Deliverable: one-pager with charts. ETA 2027-01-05.
- Logan: assemble SOW template with an explicit data handling clause (de-identification) and proposed acceptance tests for latency and throughput. I will route the first draft to Emily + Samir by 2026-12-21.

Logistics: I'll create a HubSpot deal and folder (link below) and include the SOW draft + the SOC2 extract when available. If CFO timeline changes, we'll fallback to a tightly-scoped hosted pilot that meets encryption and access controls while legal completes review.

HubSpot: https://hubspot.redwood.com/deal/DEAL-9087-AURELIA
Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0Bz-aurelia-pilot-materials

Thanks — I’ll kick off the doc work now.
